item.title: Self-Hosted SDN Controllers: ONOS vs OpenDaylight vs Floodlight (2026)
item.description: Software-Defined Networking (SDN) decouples the control plane from the data plane, enabling centralized network programmability through standardized protocols like OpenFlow. At the heart of any SDN deployment sits the SDN controller — the “network operating system” that manages flow rules, discovers topology, and exposes programmable APIs for network automation.

item.title: OpenDaylight vs Faucet vs Ryu: Self-Hosted SDN Controllers Compared 2026
item.description: Software-Defined Networking (SDN) separates the control plane from the data plane, giving you centralized, programmable control over your entire network infrastructure. Instead of configuring each switch individually, an SDN controller manages flow rules across all devices from a single point.
